name: Patient records pointers
definition: Pointers to health data (not data itself).
challenges: Privacy and consent are strictly regulated (e.g. GDPR, HIPAA); storing or processing health data on public infrastructure raises legal and ethical questions. Consent must be informed, specific, and revocable; enforcement across many systems is hard. Proving who accessed what and when is often lacking; patients may not know where their data lives or who has access.
opportunities: Pointer registry—recording where data lives and who has been given access, with tamper-evident timestamps—supports access control and audit without storing health data on-chain. Attestation of access and usage can support accountability and compliance. Consent receipts and usage policies can be anchored for verification; GDPR-compliant designs are being piloted in health data spaces.

experiments.title: HL7 FHIR + verifiable credentials
experiments.description: Healthcare interoperability with provider credential verification.
